task_reconstruction.official_task: Place a charging network and forecast the electric-vehicle market.

section_map.summary: Coverage program converted to a flow.

contributions.summary: A coverage program solved as a min-cost flow.
A game that sets the pile-to-car cutoff.

dependency_graph.handoff: the charger count the ratio is measured against
the adoption timeline the investment must match

assumptions.summary: Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and home charging excluded.
Urban and suburban zones treated as circles.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Tesla addresses geocoded through the Google API.
Demand from average miles driven per state and census urban areas.

models.summary: Coverage solved as a min-cost flow.
A game sets the build cutoff.

verification.summary: The cutoff checked against six years of US data.
The Bass curve matches Korean sales since 2012.

results_trace.summary: Build piles below a ratio of 0.275.

writing_logic.summary: Three facets named before any model.
The slow form is named, then the equivalent form.
The reader gets a factor list, not a single recommendation.

language_observations.summary: Equilibrium turned into a one-cutoff rule.

visualization_observations.summary: Figures 3 to 5 map US charger distribution, connections and a contour.
Figures 10 and 11 plot adoption and cumulative potential.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Stating the reformulation lets a judge see why the flow replaces the program.

independent_extensions.summary: Print the fitted Bass coefficients p and q.

candidate_rule_impacts.impact: Adoption dated by a diffusion hazard.
Chargers placed on a geocoded graph.
One cutoff sets the build order.
Nodes geocoded from a named source.
Equilibrium checked on six years of data.
Conflicting node counts kept side by side.
Two timelines kept side by side.
